name: WebRTC data channels (peer to peer)
plain: Sends data directly between browsers without a server, with no prompt.
meaning: A site can connect two people peer to peer. Setup exchanges network candidates, which can expose the person's public IP address to the other peer or to the site.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: No iframe flag; permissions policy applies only to camera and microphone
steps: Create RTCPeerConnection with STUN or TURN
Exchange SDP and ICE candidates via signaling

limits.headline: Can send data straight between two browsers, with no pop up
limits.user_action: Nothing for data. A video call asks for camera permission only when you use it.
can: Send text, files or game moves straight to another person's browser
Keep the connection open while the pages are open
Connect two people through a quick set up over the internet
cannot: Reach your camera or microphone without a separate permission
Stay connected after you close the page
Work with no server at all; a server helps the two browsers meet
Always hide your network address from the other person

story.what_it_is: Two browsers can send data straight to each other, with no prompt.

marketing.name: WebRTC
marketing.pitch: The WebRTC project says it brings real time communication to browsers through simple APIs.

story.for_you: You never see it. In a video call or a browser game, your device may talk directly to another person's device. That can reveal your network address to the other side.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for real time speed and to save server costs. It powers file sharing, games and calls. It can also expose your real network address even behind a VPN, which fraud teams use to spot you.

use_cases.example: A browser multiplayer game sends player moves directly between players for low delay.
A video call app sends your voice and video peer to peer when it can.
A web file sharing tool sends a large file straight to a friend with no upload.
A live Xbox Cloud Gaming or GeForce NOW stream uses the same family of tech to send the picture.
A fraud tool uses it to learn a visitor's real network address and spot a VPN.
A shared code editor syncs edits straight between teammates.

technical_bounds: No prompt for data-only connections; camera or mic needs getUserMedia
Local IP candidates hidden behind mDNS .local names (Chrome 75, Safari 11, Firefox 78) unless media permission is granted
STUN reveals the public IP to peers and to the STUN server
Max message size: Chrome about 256 KiB, Firefox up to 1 GiB (maxMessageSize)
Ordered or unordered, reliable or partially reliable; SCTP over DTLS

abuse: Peer to peer botnet or proxy networks

history.change: mDNS host candidates hide local IPs
